title.narrative: Improved policy formulation and advocacy to support youth employment and training in the country

description.narrative:
Timor-Leste faces ongoing development challenges, including high youth unemployment, limited economic opportunities—especially in rural areas—and a disconnect between training systems and labour market needs. Women and youth are particularly vulnerable to unemployment and underemployment. The country’s Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system is currently unable to adequately meet labour market demands, especially in agroforestry.
To address this, the ILO, with EU funding, is supporting sustainable economic growth and decent job creation through improved skills development and labour market integration in selected agroforestry value chains. This initiative is implemented in close coordination with SEFOPE, relevant ministries, training institutions, private sector representatives, trade unions, and the Chamber of Commerce and Industry. Key priorities include aligning TVET curricula with market demands, building capacity among training providers and instructors, and strengthening employment services.
The ILO also assists SEFOPE’s National Employment Strategy Secretariat in developing an action-oriented implementation plan, detailing responsibilities, timelines, and resource needs.
Further, the ILO supports a Green Employment Diagnostic to facilitate a Just Transition. This study identifies green job opportunities, evaluates vulnerable sectors, and supports policy directions for a more sustainable, environmentally aligned labour market.
